title: Retrying Requests with Backoff
hints: Loop: try the operation, and on a retryable error sleep then try again.
`catch where attempt < maxAttempts && isRetryable(error)` retries; otherwise the error escapes.
jsBridge: Retry with exponential backoff and a retryability check is the same as JS's `p-retry`, written as a generic `async` function with `Task.sleep`, which also respects cancellation.

compass.q: `p-retry` in JS vs a hand-written Swift `retry`: what does `Task.sleep` give you that `setTimeout` promises don't (cancellation)?
Which errors are retryable? A 400? A 503? `URLError.notConnectedToInternet`?
Exponential backoff vs adding jitter: why does jitter matter for millions of clients?
Retrying a non-idempotent POST (payment): what could go wrong, and what's the fix (idempotency keys)?
